newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open firm, Wall Street helps.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open firm, Wall Street helps.

text.p: Singapore shares were mostly firmer at the open on Wednesday with buying seen in selected blue chips.

Dealers said sentiment was underpined by the record close on Wall Street stocks overnight after congressional testimony from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan contained no unsettling remarks on the economy and financial markets.
"Some of the big stocks are moving today. Volume is not heavy but funds are picking up stocks like NatSteel and DBS Land," a broker with a Singapore firm said.
After about an hour of trading, the Straits Times Industrial Index was up 5.62 points to 1,956.13. Total volume was about 58 million units with 118 gainers against 40 losers.
About a third of the volume was accounted for by Asia Food & Property, which topped the actives with more than 20 million shares traded.
Dealers said 17 million shares were married at between US$1 and US$1.06. The shares were trading at US$1.07, down two cents from its previous close.
Chinese drug company Tianjin Zhongxin continued to new highs, touching US$1.64 in early dealings. It was up 11 cents at US$1.60 with over eight million traded.
Other gainers include foreign tranches of banks like UOB, OCBC and DBS, which all rose 20 cents each.
Early losers included ship repair conglomerate Keppel Corp, down 10 cents to S$6.55, and Singapore Land, which eased five cents to S$7.20.
